title: LadiesGo fire test report (Luanda launch)
method: Custom harnesses: loadtest/firetest.mjs (scaled concurrent-trips), loadtest/ws-storm.mjs (WS storm vs global DOs), wrangler tail CPU profiling, raw-connection probes.
verdict: Blocker fixed and verified. PBKDF2_ITER 100000->10000, worker redeployed (version 37948e5a-543a-49ab-ab76-39168aebb220). Post-fix: 0 x 503/1102; trip levels 20/40 = 100% (784 reqs, all 200). Remaining constraint is the single-client connection cap, not the backend.

fix.compatibility: verifyPassword reads iterations from the stored hash, so existing 100k hashes still verify; only new hashes use 10k.

verified.beforeFix: setup aborted with 503/1102 at 22-54 requests even at concurrency 1; tail showed 48/209 invocations exceededCpu
verified.afterFix_levels_50_100: 0 x 503; failures were client-side TypeError (fetch failed) due to the ~30 new-connection client cap

headlineFindings.finding: Under sustained auth/DB load the Worker returns HTTP 503 with Cloudflare error 1102 ('Worker exceeded CPU time limit'). Happened in all scaled runs, even with setup concurrency 1 (serial).

evidence.page042Docs: error 1102 == Worker exceeded CPU time limit

headlineFindings.rootCauseHypothesis: index.ts:56 PBKDF2_ITER=100000. Every login/register/reset/admin-driver-create runs 100k PBKDF2-SHA256 via WebCrypto, giving 15-46ms CPU per request; under bursts it crosses the configured CPU limit (~50ms) -> 1102.
recommendations: Reduce PBKDF2_ITER from 100000 to 10000 (10x CPU cut) OR move hashing off the hot path.
Confirm Workers plan and raise/Set CPU limit (wrangler.toml [limits] cpu_ms) on a paid plan.
Add client retry/backoff for 503 as mitigation.

headlineFindings.finding: Three global singleton Durable Objects are single points of contention at Luanda scale: RequestsHub (requests:global), DriverGeo (geo:global), TripRinger (global). All traffic for all cities in Angola hits one instance each.
recommendations: Load-test with a distributed generator (single client is insufficient; see CLIENT-CAP).

headlineFindings.finding: A single client from this environment cannot open more than ~26-36 concurrent NEW TLS connections to Cloudflare: 50 concurrent raw HTTPS to cloudflare.com and to the worker -> ~28 ok / 22 stalled; identical 50 to google.com -> 50 ok. So it is the client->Cloudflare path, not the backend. HTTP keep-alive works (100 concurrent trips ok).
recommendations: Use a distributed load generator (k6 cloud, multiple VMs/IPs, or a Cloudflare Worker-based generator) for true 5000-concurrent tests.

headlineFindings.finding: WebSocket handshake to the DO path costs ~1.1-1.4s each sequentially (pong RTT only ~340ms). 50 concurrent handshakes -> only ~30 succeed (mostly the client cap above). Not yet proven as a backend defect.
recommendations: Re-run from a distributed generator to separate connection-establishment cost from the client cap.

headlineFindings.finding: Prior validated run: 100 concurrent full trip lifecycles (request->accept->arrived->pin->start->complete) = 100% success, 100% HTTP 200, ~919 trips/min, no errors. p50 lifecycle ~5.6s (network RTT dominated: edge -AMS).

sideEffects: Test runs created several hundred driver/passenger accounts and some trips in production D1. No delete endpoint; trips were cancelled. Consider cleanup SQL.
nextSteps: Fix PBKDF2/CPU (blocker), redeploy, re-run firetest.mjs setup.
Set up staging (2nd Worker + 2nd D1 via [env.staging]) to avoid polluting production.
Run distributed 5000-concurrent WS+HTTP test and capture Cloudflare Workers Metrics (Exceeded CPU / Exceeded Memory charts).
Shard the three singleton DOs by city/geocell.
